lemmas.statement: The Route C landing premise (any MUB quadruple in C^6 is unitarily equivalent to one containing F_6 or a Haagerup deformation) implies there is no complete set of 7 MUBs in C^6.
Any MUB6 orbit configuration has at least 15 Fourier landing edges (n_dita + pairCombinations n_dita >= 15). This is a counting fact and does not prove the landing claim.
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem edges_ge_15 (cfg : MUB6.RouteC.MUB6OrbitConfiguration) : 15 ≤ cfg.n_dita + MUB6.RouteC.pairCombinations cfg.n_dita := MUB6.RouteC.fourier_landing_edges_lower_bound cfg

near_misses.claim: The landing premise follows from the edge-count lower bound of 15.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The edge-count bound is purely combinatorial; it gives no algebraic or unitary-equivalence classification of MUB quadruples in C^6.

near_misses.claim: The Wootters field/character bound of 3 MUBs gives the landing for dimension 6.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: 6 is not a prime power, so the field construction does not apply, and the bound of 3 is not a classification of arbitrary quadruples.

open_obligations: No concrete algebraic landing theorem or chart interpretation exists for the quadruple-to-F_6/Haagerup statement.
No generators grounded: all SRC declarations are theorems, defs or structures rather than typed operations with known colours.
Haagerup deformation family is not formalised in the cited sources.
Classification of all MUB quadruples up to unitary equivalence is not available.
